findings.scenario: mid-restore purge-ledger append (the restore-side TOCTOU): the claimed SERIALIZABLE repair does not serialize against the realistic concurrent ledger writer
findings.evidence: my blocking probe (fresh scratch DBs; the insert phase widened with per-row pg_sleep(0.03) BEFORE-INSERT triggers on the ten inserted tables; the restore launched as a subprocess; a read-committed arv_app INSERT into arv.purge_ledger for the note fired at +0.5s and +0.65s): iteration 0 — the writer's psql exited (its autocommit INSERT committed) at t=0.511s, the restore exited rc=0 at t=0.837s with the note FULLY PRESENT (2 revisions), the ledger row present, and the completion printing ledger_as_of=empty; iteration 1 — writer at 0.661s, restore rc=0 at 0.834s, same state. That is the round-1 defect verbatim: a restore committed on top of a ledger write that committed BEFORE the restore's commit, leaving the permanent purged-but-present state with no re-reconciliation path. ROOT CAUSE characterized with minimal two-session psql probes: a SERIALIZABLE reader whose snapshot precedes a read-committed writer's commit COMMITS CLEANLY (a lone rw-edge reader->writer forms no cycle; SSI only aborts on cycles), and still commits when the reader also writes the table with disjoint rows — so the typed ARV-EXP-007 serialization branch is UNREACHABLE for a plain single-INSERT ledger writer (the governed purge command's own class), and no table lock exists to block it. The suite's EXP-11 pin cannot detect this: its order_b branch (rc=0, note present, ledger=1) performs NO ordering discrimination and the test launches the writer BEFORE the restore. A correct repair is e.g. LOCK TABLE arv.purge_ledger IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE inside the transaction before the re-read (the writer then always lands before-the-read or after-the-commit), or an advisory-lock/retry protocol
findings.status_note: fix before merge: hold an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on arv.purge_ledger across the reconciliation's re-read and the insert phase (or otherwise prove the write cannot interleave); strengthen EXP-11 to discriminate the interleaved order (the writer must provably commit either before the re-read or after the restore's exit)

review_summary: ROUND 2, FRESH CONTEXT. The round-1 P2-class repairs verify under my own independent probes: F2 (the ledger merge) — the both-sides-key restore completes rc=0 with the destination's 'DEST-ENTRY' preserved, one ledger row, the entity dropped; F3 (the highlight cascade) — the highlight, its lifecycle, and the inbound references drop while the note survives both revisions; F5 (the clean gate) — a stray no-command_log note row refuses ARV-EXP-002 untouched. The core re-verifies clean on fresh scratch databases: the 13-table export/restore equality is byte-exact through arv_read under my own richer TSV forms; the note+source purge permanence holds (the whole capture tree absent, work/command_log intact); the dropped-ledger destination fails closed ARV-EXP-006; the tampered manifest refuses ARV-EXP-003; the suite runs GREEN once (exit 0, EXP-01..14) and the LAW-05/red trail verifies (322/559/1 within limits; the f6cf5fb binding chains through two amendments to the on-disk digest 8995bb07, with red-02.txt recording EXP-12/13/14 RED at e006897). BUT the round-1 P1 F1 repair is UNSOUND and the defect persists: my blocking probe (restore-first, the writer fired mid-insert-phase) reproduced the interleaved defect in 2 of 6 interleavings — a read-committed arv_app ledger INSERT committed 0.17-0.33s BEFORE the restore's rc=0 exit, the note restored fully present, the completion printing ledger_as_of=empty: a restore committed on top of an un-reconciled ledger write (the permanent purged-but-present state, SYS-10's hole). Root cause proven minimally: SERIALIZABLE cannot abort on a lone rw-edge from a read-committed writer (no cycle), so the promised ARV-EXP-007 branch is unreachable for the realistic writer class and no table lock blocks the write; EXP-11's pin cannot catch it (order_b checks no ordering; the writer fires before the restore). ONE NEW P2 (F6): anchor-kind ledger entries (permitted by migration 0013's CHECK) drop only the anchor row — the anchored highlights/bookmarks survive the reconciliation and the insert phase dies on the dangling FK, refusing the WHOLE archive (the coarse-refusal class F3's repair eliminated for highlights). DISPOSITION: BLOCKED on the open P1 F1 (fix: hold an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on arv.purge_ledger across the reconciliation re-read and the insert phase, and strengthen EXP-11 to discriminate the interleaved order); F6 should be fixed or explicitly routed in the same pass.
